name: capture-model
thesis: Classification belongs to the procedure, not to the manifest. Today a manifest asks for a persistence mode and Forge checks that request against one hard-coded seven-path allowlist (forge/src/storage/captures.mjs:58-66); Builder asks for nothing and stores every body (builder_bundle.js:361-366). Neither is a classification model. This option makes every read carry a tier that a repository-owned, reviewed, drift-gated classification file assigns to its procedure path, and makes the exported persistence the MINIMUM of what the manifest asked for and what the tier allows. A manifest can only ever ask for less than its tier, never more, and the projection happens at read time so an unprojected protected body never reaches IndexedDB at all. That closes P-10 to P-14 without removing an allowlist, and it closes P-58 by separating four claims the bundle conflates today: the read happened, the record exists, a body was kept, and a body may leave the device. The decisive evidence that three tiers are not enough is already committed: harvests/inbox/tnr_results_1789189076617.json holds 1.5 MB of combat.getBattleEntries bodies whose `description` and `appliedEffects[].txt` embed other players' usernames inside free prose, which no field allowlist can redact - so a local-only tier with an exported hash, not a projection, is the only honest home for that shape.

tiers.name: repo-safe
tiers.what_data: Decoded bodies of audited game-CONTENT record and content-vocabulary reads: records this repository authored or that describe the content catalogue. No user, account, session or other-player field by construction.
tiers.where_it_may_persist: bundle in the public repository (plus the immutable IndexedDB capture_snapshots copy the bundle is materialized from, forge/src/storage/captures.mjs:238-250)
tiers.export_rules: Full decoded body exported as `data`. Export re-reads the snapshot, never the game, never the path+id read cache (forge/src/ui/app.mjs:339-366; the FFC-1 aliasing reason is written out at captures.mjs:13-25). Per-body ceiling stays the existing MAX_FULL_CAPTURE_BYTES 512 KiB (captures.mjs:84); over it is an explicit persistence FAILURE, never truncation (runner.mjs:614).
tiers.redaction: None, because no field in scope carries identity. Enforced negatively by a test, not by trust: no path whose registry `auth` is "protected" may carry tier repo-safe without an explicit director ruling recorded in the classification entry's `rationale` (the test reads forge/src/transport/procedures.mjs and the classification projection, the same construction as forge/test/storage.captures.test.mjs:78 'every full-persistence path is an audited content-record point read, and nothing else is').
tiers.retention: The IDB snapshot is immutable, never invalidated by a write (captures.mjs:22-25), deleted only by explicit per-key or per-job action (captures.mjs:262-273). The bundle in git is permanent; removing one is a director decision about repository history, not a tool action.
tiers.ui_before_the_read_runs: Preflight states a count and a destination in the same line as the run button: 'N record bodies will be committed to the public repository'. Tier chip on every capture row uses the existing --acc outlined construction from D_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md (information), never --ok: --ok is reserved for verdicts (VERIFIED, DONE-success, 'body persisted') and reusing it for a classification is exactly the pill reuse A_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.md §A.7 BF-25 records as the breach to stop. No new palette, no second shell.
tiers.who_may_request_it: Any manifest, but only for a path the classification file already places at this tier. A request above tier is a ManifestError before the job opens, the same construction as the existing persist:"full" refusals (forge/src/runner/manifest.mjs:129-137).
example_procedures: gameAsset.get, jutsu.get, item.get, bloodline.get, quests.get, profile.getAi, ai.getAiProfile - the seven that are FULL_PERSIST_PATHS today (captures.mjs:58-66); P-14 FORGE BETTER, keep-in-forge

ai.getAiRelations (ai.ts:165, publicProcedure, 'quests referencing an AI') - the dependency read a publish flip needs before it hides or shows a record; H R-08 names the missing check, C.2c row 'all classes'

tiers.name: projected
tiers.what_data: Bodies whose useful content is a small, named, non-identity subset of a larger or protected body: list and paged reads, name lists, and research reads whose identity fields can be dropped or aliased.
tiers.where_it_may_persist: projected fields only, in the bundle in the public repository. The unprojected body is never written to capture_snapshots and never written to the read cache.
tiers.export_rules: The manifest declares `persist:"fields"` and `fields:[...]`. Every requested field must be in the classification entry's `fields` allowlist; a field outside it is a ManifestError before the job opens. Projection is applied in the runner immediately after the read returns and before any store call (the insertion point is beside forge/src/runner/runner.mjs:597 _persistFull), so the store layer never holds the whole body. Refusal on an unprojectable body shape: if the entry declares `rowsAt` (for a paged envelope) and the body does not match, nothing is stored and `persistError` names the shape - it does not fall through to storing the body.
tiers.redaction: Three declared operators only, never a heuristic (H R-04's mitigation line: 'redaction is a manifest-declared projection, never a heuristic'): `drop` (omit the field, which is the default since an unlisted field cannot be selected), `hash` (stable digest, so two rows about the same opponent are comparable without naming them), and `pseudonym` (a per-job salted alias such as `opp-7f3a`; the salt lives in IndexedDB and is never exported). No regex scrubbing of prose is offered, because prose cannot be scrubbed safely - see the local-only tier.
tiers.retention: Only the projected rows persist; there is nothing else to retain. The projected capture is as permanent as the bundle.
tiers.ui_before_the_read_runs: 'N projected rows (K of M fields) will be committed to the public repository', with the field list itself behind disclosure and the dropped/aliased fields named. The chip is the same --acc outline plus a field count, so projected and repo-safe are distinguishable at a glance without a second hue (SCR:189 forbids making a full capture look identical to a summary one; the same argument applies between projected and full).
tiers.who_may_request_it: Any manifest, for any path the classification file places at projected or higher. A path at projected can never be asked for `persist:"full"`.
example_procedures: quests.getAllNames, jutsu.getAllNames, item.getAllNames, gameAsset.getAllNames, profile.getAllAiNames with fields [id, name, hidden] - already in the audited registry (procedures.mjs:33,39,46,52,58,66); this is the exact shape .github/scripts/build_answers.py:85-89 normalizes, and it is why zero Forge bundles have ever fed answers/ (C.2b W-14). tiers.name: local-only
tiers.what_data: Bodies that are legitimate research but cannot be made repository-safe by a field allowlist, because identity is embedded in free text rather than in fields.
tiers.where_it_may_persist: local IndexedDB only (capture_snapshots, on the operator's device).
tiers.export_rules: The bundle carries the summary entry plus `rows`, `present`, `bodyHash` and `bytes` - never `data`. `persistOk:true` here means 'the body is on this device', and the run screen and the bundle must say that in those words rather than reusing the repo-safe sentence. An export that finds the snapshot missing records persistError exactly as today (app.mjs:353-356) and does not re-read the game.
tiers.redaction: None is attempted, and that is the point: attempting it would be the heuristic R-04 forbids. The body simply does not leave the device.
tiers.retention: Never deleted automatically (the non-negotiable). The capture library shows an age and a 'stale' marker after a director-set interval and offers an explicit 'Discard local bodies for this job' action behind the deliberate confirmation SCR:346-356 already requires for snapshot deletion. Device loss loses these bodies - stated in the UI, because they are the only Forge data with no repository copy.
tiers.ui_before_the_read_runs: 'N bodies stay on this device and are NOT committed'. Chip uses the existing --hidden-fill / --hidden-text slate construction (the 'present but not published' pill Forge already owns, D_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md semantic-states table), which is exactly the meaning wanted and adds no token.
tiers.who_may_request_it: Any manifest, with `persist:"local"`. It is also the automatic downgrade target when a higher-tier entry is marked drifted.
example_procedures: combat.getBattleEntries (combat.ts:382 at pin 345d18ac, protectedProcedure). Behaviour-proven why: harvests/inbox/tnr_results_1789189076617.json is 1,523,320 bytes of these bodies and its `description` field reads 'Particle Cannon: dauntless weaves ... towards ANBU Member', with more usernames inside appliedEffects[].txt. A field allowlist that keeps `description` keeps the names; one that drops it keeps nothing useful. P-10, gate G-02
Any future protected research read whose body carries prose. The tier is the default landing place for a protected query until the director rules a projection for it (K-06/K-17).

tiers.name: transient
tiers.what_data: Reads whose answer is needed to render one screen or to pre-check one action, and whose durable copy would be a liability or a staleness trap.
tiers.where_it_may_persist: in memory only. Not the read cache, not capture_snapshots, not the journal beyond `{proc, ok, at}`.
tiers.export_rules: Never exported. A transient read may not appear in a manifest's capture list at all; it is issued by a surface, not by a manifest, and it still passes the auth gate (auth.mjs:210) and still debits the budget (bucket.mjs:169-216).
tiers.redaction: Not applicable; nothing is stored to redact.
tiers.ui_before_the_read_runs: No chip. The surface says what it is reading and that the read costs budget - the budget line Forge already renders (Budget.status(), bucket.mjs:204). No 'status light' that implies a fresh poll it did not make (H R-16).
tiers.who_may_request_it: Forge surfaces only, for a named, reviewed purpose. The first two purposes: the auth probe (profile.getAi with a sentinel id, main.mjs boot) and a publish-time dependency pre-check (ai.getAiRelations, jutsu.getJutsuRelations) whose result must never be cached, because a stale 'no quest references this AI' would be worse than no answer.
example_procedures: profile.getAi as the boot probe - already transient in effect (auth.mjs:1-30 holds a state string and booleans only; forge/test/auth.test.mjs 'the probe reads the game's answer, persists nothing'). This tier makes the existing behaviour a named category rather than a one-off.
ai.getAiRelations / jutsu.getJutsuRelations as a publish pre-check (H R-08; W-23)

allowlist_policy.where_the_classification_lives: skills/building-tnr-content/data/50_DATA_capture_classification.json in this repository, generated-projected into the bundle by forge/tools/derive_capture_classification.mjs at build time, exactly as 32b_DATA_pool.json, fields.json and nested.json are today (forge/build.mjs; A_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.md §A.6). RUL-2026-09-12-002: the repository owns the rule, Forge carries a generated projection of it and never hand-edits the projection. This is also the discipline H R-20 demands after missionDraftProblems re-encoded profile policy in JavaScript.
allowlist_policy.entry_shape: { path, kind, auth, limited, tier, shape: "record"|"list"|"page", fields: [..] | null, rowsAt: string|null, knownKeys: [..], redact: {field: "drop"|"hash"|"pseudonym"}, sourceFile, sourceLine, sourceSha, pins: {global, task}, rationale, reviewedBy, reviewedAt, ruling: "RUL-..."|null }
allowlist_policy.separation_from_the_transcribed_registry: forge/src/transport/procedures.mjs stays what its header says it is (procedures.mjs:1-22): kind, limited, mcp and auth TRANSCRIBED from the pinned source, auth recorded explicitly and never derived from limited. `tier` is policy, not transcription, and lives in the classification file so that a policy edit can never be mistaken for a source fact. The classification file's `kind`/`auth` columns are asserted equal to the registry by a test; a mismatch fails the build.
how_a_procedure_joins_a_tier: 1. Transcription: the row is added to procedures.mjs with kind/limited/mcp/auth read at the Forge global pin 345d18ac AND at the task pin bdec2883, both file:line recorded. The existing invariant test forge/test/auth.test.mjs:88 ('the auth class of every audited procedure is transcribed from source, not derived from the limiter') and :120 ('FPA-3: identical at the task pin and at Forge's global pin') then cover it for free.

2. Shape and known keys: `shape` is derived from the input schema (a required {limit,cursor} makes it a page - the rule reader.mjs:75 already states in prose). `knownKeys` is seeded from a committed body where one exists (the two combat bundles, the six paged-list bundles) and is otherwise empty, which is safe because it only feeds the drift tripwire, never the allowlist.

3. Field allowlist: `fields` is proposed by the author with a one-line reason per field and is the object of review. I do not claim it can be generated from source: deriving a Drizzle query's return shape is not demonstrated anywhere in this repository (Inferred). The tripwire below is the compensating control.

4. Review: ChatGPT independently reviews the transcription and the tier against the pinned source, the same owner B_PARITY_MATRIX.md gate G-02 already names ('Fable (Lane A) with ChatGPT review of the auth transcription'). A tier above local-only on a protected path additionally needs a director ruling id in `ruling`.
5. Ruling: the tier assignment itself is user-owned (K-06, K-17). Nothing in this option assigns a final tier; the example tiers above are recommendations with their evidence attached.

source_drift_gate.static: forge/tools/pin_relevance.mjs (already declares the host surfaces, H R-02) grows a classification pass: for every entry it hashes the procedure's source text at the game head of the day and compares to `sourceSha`. A changed hash marks the entry `drifted` in the generated projection. This runs as the phase-0 gate H R-05 already describes, on the head of the day, not on a stale pin.
source_drift_gate.runtime: An unknown-key tripwire at projection time. If a body carries a key not in `knownKeys`, the projection still emits only the allowlisted fields - so a new PII field can never leak by default - and the capture entry records `unknownKeys: ["name", ...]` (KEY NAMES ONLY, never values) and the entry's tier is reported as drifted. This is the honest answer to 'how do you know the body did not gain an identity field since the pin' without pretending the return shape is derivable.
source_drift_gate.failure_mode: A drifted entry downgrades one tier at runtime (repo-safe to projected, projected to local-only, local-only to summary) and the run screen names the reason. Fail-closed, and it means a manifest that exported yesterday may export less today with the same manifest hash - see weaknesses.
source_drift_gate.test: A new forge/test/capture.classification.test.mjs asserts: every classification path exists in PROCEDURES with the same kind/auth; no protected path carries tier repo-safe without a `ruling`; no mutation carries any tier; a drifted entry downgrades; the projection refuses a field outside `fields`; and the tripwire records names and never values. Kept green per phase alongside the existing forge/test/capture.full.test.mjs (23 tests) and storage.captures.test.mjs (13 tests).

projection_mode.manifest_surface: `{ proc, input, persist: "fields", fields: ["id","name","hidden"] }`. `select` is accepted as a read alias for `fields` so the one committed Builder manifest that uses it (push/05_aerathiel_pvp_research_stage1.json) parses unchanged.
projection_mode.validation_before_the_job_opens: In normalizeCapture (forge/src/runner/manifest.mjs:113-140), beside the existing persist:"full" checks: (a) `persist` must be one of summary|fields|full|local; (b) the path must exist in the classification projection; (c) the requested mode must be at or below the path's tier; (d) every element of `fields` must be in the entry's `fields` allowlist; (e) `fields` must be non-empty. Each failure is a ManifestError with the same message construction the file already uses, so no job is opened and no read is issued. This is the fail-closed half of the brief's section 5 requirement.
projection_mode.application_point: At read time in the runner, immediately after the reader returns and BEFORE cache.put and before putSnapshot - i.e. a `_persistFields` sibling of runner.mjs:597 _persistFull. Two consequences, both deliberate: the unprojected protected body is never written to IndexedDB at all, and the read cache holds the projected rows, so a later manifest that wants more fields must re-read and spend budget rather than silently reusing a body it should not have.
projection_mode.why_not_Builder's_construction: builder_bundle.js:355-356 capTrim returns the body UNCHANGED when it is not an array, so a `select` on a single-record body silently ships the whole record. Forge's projection handles object bodies and array bodies, uses `rowsAt` for a paged envelope, and REFUSES any other shape with a persistError rather than falling through to the whole body. Fail-closed where Builder fails open.
projection_mode.scope_honesty_derived_not_regexed: Builder derives its scope sentence from a regex on the path name (`/getAll|\.list$|Names$/i`, builder_bundle.js:369). That regex does not match combat.getBattleHistory, so the committed bundle harvests/inbox/tnr_results_1789188714166.json labels a 43-row FILTERED list as `scope: "record fetch"` - the exact class of wrong-absence claim harvest.py's header was written to prevent (harvest.py:1-14). Forge derives `scope` from the classification entry's `shape` plus whether an input was actually sent, so a filtered list is always labelled one. This turns P-13's 'evidence-safety nicety' into a defect fix.
projection_mode.journaled_input_equals_sent_input: Today runner.mjs:589 journals `input: c.input` (the manifest's) while reader.mjs:82 sends `input: undefined` for name lists - P-11's and P-58's input-honesty defect. Under this model `input` on the capture entry IS the input actually sent, `requested` carries the manifest's version only when the two differ, and a differing pair sets `inputAdjusted:true` with a reason. A test asserts journaled input === sent input for every list read, which is gate G-03's stated acceptance verbatim.
projection_mode.harvest_py_consumption: harvest.py entries() reads c['proc'], c['input'] and c['data'], falling back to c['rows'] only when data is None and rows is a list (harvest.py:47-65). Projected rows are written to `data`, so index/get/names/assets answer from a Forge bundle with NO change to harvest.py. `filtered` is derived there from `input` alone (harvest.py:60), which becomes correct for the first time once `input` is the input actually sent.
projection_mode.build_answers_py_consumption: build_answers.py:76-96 takes capture['rows'] if it is a list, else capture['data'], then normalizes each row to [id|userId, name|username, hidden] for the five paths in CAPTURE_ENTITY (build_answers.py:20-26). A projected *.getAllNames capture with fields [id, name, hidden] in `data` satisfies that exactly, with NO change to build_answers.py. This is the mechanism that lets a Forge bundle feed answers/ for the first time (today every answers/ delta row comes from a Builder bundle, C.2b W-14).
projection_mode.measured_backward_compat_contract: The 23 archived generator scripts read only three capture keys: 52 occurrences of ['data'], one of ['input'], one of ['proc'] plus 15 .get('proc') and one .get('input') (Observed, grep over archive/spent-manifests/push-2026-09-09/*.gen.py in this pass). Zero read `select` or `scope`. So the compatibility contract for projection is exactly: `data`, `proc`, `input` keep their Builder meaning. Everything else this model adds is additive and ignorable.

registry_expansion.correction_first: The registry-gap evidence (docs/forge_next/evidence/registry-gap.json, 145 rows over ai, bloodline, gameAsset, guide, item, jutsu, profile, quests, staff) does NOT contain quests.getAll, gameAsset.getAll or the five *.getAllNames, because those are already audited (procedures.mjs:33,38,39,46,52,58,65,66). P-11 and P-12 are therefore a READER and PERSISTENCE gap, not a registry gap: reader.list() refuses anything not matching /\.getAll(Ai)?Names$/ (reader.mjs:73-76) and runner._captures only derives input.id (runner.mjs:577-582). Nor does it contain the combat router at all; combat.* comes from the parity row P-10's own cites (combat.ts:382,530 at pin 345d18ac).

registry_expansion.how_the_combat_reads_used_by_push_05_and: push/05 asks for combat.getBattleHistory with an explicit select of seven fields including attackedId, defenderId, attacker and defender. Under this model that manifest parses, but `fields` is intersected with the classification allowlist: the three non-identity fields always pass, and the four identity fields pass only if the director rules them repo-committable (K-06) or, if the pseudonym operator is approved, are emitted as stable per-job aliases so the guide pass still distinguishes opponents without naming them - replacing the hand anonymisation K-06's evidence describes. push/06 asks for 43 combat.getBattleEntries reads with no select; under this model it runs at tier local-only, the 43 bodies stay in IndexedDB, and the bundle carries 43 summary entries with rows, present, bytes and bodyHash. That is less than Builder gives today and it is the honest answer: the alternative is another 1.5 MB of named players in a public repository. Whether that is acceptable, or whether push/06-shaped work stays on Builder until a projection exists, is K-06/K-17 and gate G-02's, not mine.

keys_kept_with_unchanged_meaning: captures[].input - now the input ACTUALLY SENT, which is what harvest.py:60 already assumes when it derives `filtered`
captures[].data - 52 ['data'] reads in the archived generators; the single key that decides whether the census-to-generator loop W-07 works

top-level builder, at, cfg, state, outcome, postflight, entries, captures, idmap, journal (app.mjs:376-398). validate.py never reads captures at all (grep, Observed), so nothing here touches the parity guard; R-19's checks:null defect is adjacent and stays R-19's.
keys_added_all_optional: captures[].tier - the classification actually applied: repo-safe | projected | local-only | transient
captures[].select - the projected field list, written under Builder's key name so a Builder-era reader sees what it expects; `fields` is written as an alias
captures[].scope - Builder's honesty sentence, restored but DERIVED from the entry's shape rather than a path regex
captures[].requested + .inputAdjusted - present only when the sent input differs from the manifest's

captures[].present - true|false|null. The absent-record verdict gate G-07(b) asks for. Behaviour-proven need: harvests/inbox/tnr_results_1789124514980.json captures 0, 1 and 3 are ok:true, rows:0, bytes:4, persistOk:true with data null, because profile.ts:1121-1136 returns `user ?? null`, and the job reported success with '5/5 full record bodies persisted'. Under this contract those three are present:false, they do not count toward the persisted headline, and jobOutcome (journal.mjs:76-88) does not return success unless the manifest declared the absence expected.
captures[].bodyHash - a stable digest of the full decoded body even when only fields or nothing is exported, so a local-only capture is still citable and a later re-read is comparable
captures[].unknownKeys - key NAMES only, never values; the drift tripwire's output

captures[].classificationSha - the classification revision the tier came from (RB section 6 asks every repository envelope to carry source and tool revision; this is the same discipline applied to a read)
result_harvest_contract_evolution.backward_compatibility: harvest.py verify (harvest.py:302-351) branches on cfg=='forge' or any entry carrying forgeState and on the bundle's own `outcome`; it reads no new key and ignores unknown ones, so an old harvest.py reads a v2 bundle correctly and a new bundle is still fail-closed. build_answers.py reads only rows/data and ignores the rest. The 23 archived generators read proc/input/data only. A v1 bundle read by v2-aware code has tier=null, which must render as 'classification not recorded', never as repo-safe - the ACC:123 rule that no UI may imply arbitrary captured data is repository-safe by default.
result_harvest_contract_evolution.versioning_rule: `captureContract` increments only when an EXISTING key changes meaning. Adding optional keys does not. The one key whose meaning changes in v2 is `input` (manifest's -> sent), which is why this is v2 and not an unversioned addition; the change is strictly toward honesty, and the pair `requested`/`inputAdjusted` preserves what was lost. Forge refuses to read a bundle whose captureContract is higher than its own, mirroring journal.mjs:404-423's refusal of a newer journal.
result_harvest_contract_evolution.new_tests: forge/test/harvest.test.mjs grows: a projected name-list bundle feeds build_answers.py to a byte-identical answers/hot.json (the G-03 acceptance shape); a local-only bundle carries no data and harvest.py verify still agrees with Forge's outcome; a present:false point read makes harvest.py verify print UNVERIFIED and exit 1 (gate G-07(b) verbatim). These extend the 8 existing harvest tests rather than replacing them.

never_persisted_anywhere: Session and credential material. Already enforced and must not be weakened: AuthState holds a state string and booleans (auth.mjs:1-30); CookieSession's header allowlist excludes authorization (session.mjs:38); forge/test/auth.test.mjs asserts 'no credential extraction path exists anywhere in src/' and 'nothing auth-derived is written to storage or to an exported bundle'. The classification model adds no path that could carry a token and a test forbids one.
Other players' account state: the whole staff router, profile.getUser (profile.ts:548), profile.getBlacklist (:394), profile.getSeichiSilverForStaff (:2274) - tier never.
The operator's own inventory, loadouts, ownership and quest history (the twelve per-user reads listed under registry_expansion.never) - tier never. A content tool has no content reason to hold them.
privacy_review.already_in_the_public_repository_today: This is not hypothetical. harvests/inbox/tnr_results_1789188714166.json capture 0 holds 43 rows of Clerk user ids (user_37qazcrgUPldBPI65bb25DQiCjz, user_2SA9nim7cp7JtISJo1G4I9SkHVW), usernames (dauntless, SasukeUchiha) and avatar URLs; harvests/inbox/tnr_results_1789189076617.json holds 1,523,320 bytes of battle-log bodies with usernames inside description prose. Both were committed by Builder v4.32 on 2026-09-12 (Behaviour-proven, read in this pass). The model prevents the next one; whether the existing two stay is a director decision about repository history and is surfaced, not acted on.
privacy_review.head_router_examples_that_set_the_bounda: The registry-gap evidence is drawn from the content, guide and staff routers at the Forge pin with head cross-check (registry-gap.json provenance). Read as a privacy list rather than a capability list it says: of 145 unregistered procedures, 85 are mutations that must never be callable; of the 60 queries, the great majority are per-user reads whose payload is a person, not content. Only about a dozen (the relation, evolution, folder, tag and scene-asset reads) are content-shaped. That ratio is the argument for a tier ON THE PATH rather than a mode in the manifest: the default for an unclassified path must be refusal, and it is.
privacy_review.prose_is_unredactable: combat.getBattleEntries proves that a field allowlist is not a privacy control when identity is interpolated into text the server generates. The model's answer is a tier, not a cleverer filter. No regex scrubbing is offered anywhere, which is the same rule H R-04's mitigation states and the same reason R-21 gives for refusing prose-coupled classification.
privacy_review.read_cache_hygiene: The read cache gets a tier column too, so a never/transient path can never land in it. Separately, App.loadPicker writes GitHub manifest text into the game read cache under a synthetic path github.contents (app.mjs:198-200) where the Captures screen lists it as a capture and Clear all deletes it (A_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.md section A.5, 'a design smell'). Under a classification model that store is a classified game-read store and repository text does not belong in it; moving the picker cache out is a phase-0 item already on A.12's 'what must move below the seam' list.
privacy_review.what_the_ui_must_never_say: No surface may describe a tier as a security guarantee about the GAME. H R-31 establishes that hidden is a listing and play gate, not confidentiality. The tiers in this model are about what leaves the operator's device into a public git repository, and the copy must say that and only that.

user_decisions: K-06 (open, blocks phase 1): the tier assigned to each path. Nothing here assigns a final tier. The sharpest sub-question the evidence forces: may other players' Clerk user ids, usernames and avatar URLs be committed to a public repository at all, given 43 rows of them already are?

K-17 (open, blocks phase 1): which procedures join the registry. This option recommends the K-17 option (a) shape - only procedures a committed manifest has used - plus the small set of public content-relation reads that a publish dependency check needs, and names the tier for each; the list is a proposal.
New, routed to K-06: whether the pseudonym redaction operator is acceptable for guide research, or whether aliasing an opponent is itself a record about a person that should not be committed.

New, routed to K-06: the ceiling for a projected or list body. MAX_FULL_CAPTURE_BYTES 512 KiB was sized against a 71 KB worst-case single record (captures.mjs:74-78); a 500-row projected list is a different object and needs its own number and its own over-ceiling behaviour.

New, routed to K-06/K-16: retention and staleness for local-only bodies. They are the only Forge data with no repository copy, 'no automatic deletion' is a non-negotiable, and a phone's IndexedDB is not unbounded.

New, routed to the director as a repository-history question: whether tnr_results_1789189076617.json and tnr_results_1789188714166.json remain in the public repository as committed. This option does not propose touching git history.

New, routed to K-17/G-02: whether push/06-shaped work (43 unprojected protected bodies) runs in Forge at tier local-only with a hash-only bundle, or stays on Builder until a projection exists. This is the row that decides whether gate G-02 can close.

weaknesses: The `fields` allowlist is authored and reviewed, not derived. I could not demonstrate that a Drizzle query's return shape is derivable from the pinned source the way fields.json and nested.json are derived from input schemas (Inferred). The unknown-key tripwire is a compensating control, not a substitute: it catches a NEW key, it does not catch a key that was always there and was wrongly allowlisted. That makes the review step load-bearing.

Projecting at read time means the read cache no longer holds the full body, so a later manifest that wants one more field must re-read and spend limiter budget (H R-03). On a limited path at margin 0.5 that is a real cost, and it is paid to keep the unprojected body off the device.

A drifted entry downgrades a tier at runtime, so the same manifest with the same hash can export less today than yesterday. That is fail-closed and correct, but it breaks 'same manifest, same bundle' and the manifest hash does not change (manifest.mjs:102-109 hashes the request, not the classification). The reason must be rendered on the run screen and recorded on the capture entry, and reviewers must expect it.

local-only closes P-10 for combat.getBattleEntries only in the sense that the read can happen in Forge; it does NOT close W-07 for that shape, because a repository session cannot read a body that never left the phone. The census-to-generator loop is closed only for projectable shapes (name lists, paged content lists). Whether that is enough for gate G-02 is a user decision, not a claim I can make.

Four tiers plus four persist modes is more manifest surface than one boolean allowlist, and a manifest author has one more thing to get wrong. The mitigation is that every default is the safe one (omitted persist is summary, unclassified path is refusal, out-of-allowlist field is a parse error) - but a friendlier surface here is exactly where a future change could fail open.
bodyHash on a local-only capture is only useful if someone re-reads and compares. It makes the capture citable; it does not make it reviewable by an agent working in the repository.

Nothing here was verified in a browser. IndexedDB behaviour for accumulating local-only bodies on Firefox Android is unmeasured, and whether navigator.storage.persist() is granted there is unverified (A_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.md section A.5, Inferred). A phone that evicts the tab loses local-only evidence with no repository copy, which is a sharper consequence than any eviction Forge has today.

The pseudonym operator needs a stable salt to be useful across runs, and a salt that is stable across runs is a durable record about identifiable people held on the device. I have stated the tension rather than resolved it, because resolving it is K-06's.
I did not re-derive registry-gap.json's 145 rows against the game head myself; I read the committed evidence file and its provenance block. Its own note says evidence is not automatic truth.
